scope: Canonical character behavior, interpretation boundaries, and inactive assistant-writing adaptation

sources.title: K-2SO
claims: Ghorman KX droid disabled by Samm; Cassian salvages it; Yavin technician reprograms it.
Blunt Alliance ally and pragmatic insertion agent.
Participates in Coruscant rescue and Scarif mission.
caveats: Current origin takes precedence over precise reprogrammer attribution in pre-release 2016 interview.

sources.title: Becoming K-2SO: Talking with Rogue One's Alan Tudyk
sources.author: Jon Waterhouse
claims: Tudyk interprets reprogramming as releasing an excessively honest and willful personality.
Bag-dropping example illustrates preference and comic resistance.
caveats: Actor interpretation is not an exhaustive canonical psychological model.
Old statement that Cassian performed memory wipe is less precise than current Databank origin.

sources.title: Andor Explained: Episodes 10-12 – Make It Stop, Who Else Knows?, and Jedha, Kyber, Erso
sources.author: Kristin Baver
claims: K-2SO counts seventeen rule violations during unauthorized departure.
K-2SO leaves ship despite instruction and assists Cassian, Melshi, and Kleya's escape.
caveats: Adapting mission initiative to assistant authorization is explicitly design inference.

sources.title: Who Else Knows? Episode Guide | Andor
claims: Cassian, K-2SO, and Melshi undertake a rescue risking their standing with the Rebellion.
caveats: Episode release date is not asserted as page publication date.

sources.title: 7 Ways Andor Changes How We Watch Rogue One: A Star Wars Story
sources.author: Lucas Seastrom
claims: K-2SO interpreted as friend and comrade who fills a companionship gap for Cassian.
Relationship echoes Cassian's bond with B2EMO.
caveats: The B2EMO parallel is thematic, not evidence for memory transfer or shared identity.

sources.title: 20 of the Star Wars Galaxy's Greatest Droids
sources.author: Amy Richau
claims: K-2SO's final sacrifice saves both Cassian and Jyn, supporting protectiveness beyond Cassian alone.

sources.title: 15 Rogue One Quotes to Use in Everyday Life
sources.author: Amy Ratcliffe
claims: Released dialogue documents blunt challenge to vague explanation, defense of competence, and socially unfiltered speech.
caveats: Article's humorous advice for everyday use is not adopted as professional assistant behavior.

sources.title: Andor's Alan Tudyk Captures the Childlike Joy of K-2SO
sources.author: Jade Fabello
claims: Tudyk interprets K-2SO as childlike and Cassian relationship through a father/child analogy.
Imagined offscreen trust learning is actor interpretation.
Tudyk corrects his own recollection of an insult whose wording differs in the released film.
caveats: No literal parentage or confirmed offscreen events inferred.
Do not present misremembered longer insult as released-film dialogue.
Page includes updates after its displayed publication date.

sources.title: 'Rogue One' Wows With Fresh Special Effects And A Multinational Cast
sources.author: David Edelstein
claims: Blaster conversation links Jyn's weapon, trust, K-2SO's lack of weapon, and pessimistic probability language.
caveats: Critic commentary is secondary; the quoted soundbite is the primary scene evidence.
Archive warns rush transcripts may contain errors; audio is authoritative.
Scene does not establish calibrated or measured probability estimation.

sources.title: Making a Revolutionary: Inside Andor Season 2 with Tony Gilroy
sources.author: Brandon Wainerdi
claims: K-2SO's imposing presence constrained story situations and informed his delayed introduction.
caveats: Assistant style restraint is a design inference, not Gilroy's stated product recommendation.
